input.question: Light Reflection : To maximize bedroom light, do I turn the bathroom light on or close the bathroom door? [w/ Diagram]
input.ground_truth: Well, this is a problem that can only really be solved by experiment! Especially since we have no idea about a lot of the factors involved (the exact geometry of the rooms, the exact optical properties of the paint/wallpaper, etc etc). The simplest way to measure I can think of would be to use my DSLR with a set exposure time and just take pictures of my desk with the door open and then closed, since that's a fairly objective way to measure how bright it is. If you don't have a DSLR, have fun, come up with your own experiment. Isolate what you're trying to measure as best you can and have at it!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Light Reflection : To maximize bedroom light, do I turn the bathroom light on or close the bathroom door? [w/ Diagram]

Answer:

response.prediction:
Let’s imagine your bedroom and bathroom are next to each other, like two rooms side by side.

If you want more light in your bedroom, you should **close the bathroom door**. 

Here’s why:  
If the bathroom light is on and the door is **open**, the light can escape from the bathroom and go into the hallway or your bedroom, but some of it will also go outside or just get lost in the air. When you **close the bathroom door**, more of that light stays inside the bathroom and can shine under the door into your bedroom, making your bedroom brighter.

So, to get the most light in your bedroom from the bathroom light, **turn the bathroom light on and close the bathroom door**. The light will shine under the door and make your bedroom brighter!
